finding: The new stop-signal case of CG-04-IT-16 fails now and then under load, although crap-score behaves correctly. The stub of _stoppable logs backend-start before it sets its trap for SIGTERM. The test sends the signal as soon as it sees backend-start. When crap-score forwards SIGTERM to the group before the stub reaches the trap line, the stub dies without the line backend-stopped, and the expected log does not match. The review saw it twice: once in three rounds of the timing tests with pytest -n 6 beside 18 busy loops, and once in 24 scratch runs of the HUP case. In the scratch run crap-score exited 129, the stub logged neither backend-stopped nor backend-end, and the second run started only after the stub had died, so no run overlapped. Fix: in _stoppable, set the trap before the line that logs the start, so backend-start means that the trap is in place.
why_this_severity: The test exists only on the feature branch, so it is not in use. When it passes, it checks that a stopped run stops its command before the next run starts, and its failures come from the stub, not from crap-score (no to fails_purpose). A failure in the gate-check step or at the merge costs a rerun and a search for a fault that the code does not have.
